# ROM Access Multiplexer Behavioral Specification

## 1. Purpose

This module controls which of two requesters may use a shared ROM read port:

- the system bus, which performs normal ROM reads after boot, and
- the ROM checker, which performs the startup ROM integrity check.

The module forwards address and request signals to the ROM side and routes the returned read data to the appropriate requester.

## 2. Reset and Initial State

After reset, the module shall:

- give ownership of the ROM port to the ROM checker,
- not assert a valid read response to the bus,
- not assert the alert output.

The module shall remain in this checker-owner state until the ownership input requests bus ownership.

## 3. Ownership Selection and One-Way Transfer

The ownership selection input has two levels:

- one level selects the ROM checker as the owner,
- the other level selects the bus as the owner.

The module shall support exactly one ownership transition: from checker ownership to bus ownership.

Once the bus-owner level has been sampled, the module shall remain in bus-owner state until reset. A later return to the checker-owner level shall be treated as an error condition and shall cause the alert output to be asserted.

## 4. Address and Request Forwarding

The instantaneous forwarding of the ROM address and ROM request shall follow the current ownership selection input.

When the checker-owner level is selected:

- the ROM address shall be driven from the checker address input,
- the ROM request shall be asserted continuously,
- the bus request shall be ignored,
- the bus grant output shall be deasserted.

When the bus-owner level is selected:

- the ROM address shall be driven from the bus address input,
- the ROM request shall follow the bus request input,
- the bus grant output shall be asserted.

The module shall not modify, scramble, or otherwise interpret the address. It shall simply forward the selected address unchanged.

## 5. Read Data Routing

The ROM side supplies two versions of the read data:

- a scrambled/raw version, and
- a descrambled/clear version.

The module shall:

- forward the scrambled/raw version to the ROM checker, and
- forward the descrambled/clear version to the bus.

No data transformation, checking, or validation shall be performed by this module.

## 6. Bus Read Response

The bus read-valid output shall be asserted only when:

- the ROM read-valid input is asserted, and
- the module has already recorded the transition to bus-owner state.

This masking prevents a read response generated for the ROM checker from being presented as a valid bus read response.

The bus-side read data output is meaningful only when the bus read-valid output is asserted.

## 7. Alert Behavior

The alert output shall assert when the ownership selection input requests checker ownership after the module has already recorded bus ownership.

While this error condition is present:

- the alert output shall remain asserted,
- the recorded bus-owner state shall not be cleared,
- the alert output shall deassert when the ownership input returns to the bus-owner level, or when reset is applied.

During normal checker-owner operation before any transfer to bus ownership has occurred, the alert output shall not assert.
